problem: The previous loop incorrectly treated the retriever manifest's 512-token query limit as a symmetric document limit. The official BrowseComp-Plus reproduction recipe instead encodes documents at 4096 tokens, while the downloaded prebuilt-index repository publishes vector shards and hashes but no preprocessing metadata that binds the historical vectors to that recipe.
simplest_baseline: Without loading the embedding model or issuing a search, replay only the pinned tokenizer preprocessing documented by the official 4096-token corpus-encoding recipe and measure whether every normalized literal answer atom survives in at least one gold document per case.
hypothesis: At least four of seven persistent dense misses will retain a literal answer inside a 4096-token gold-document input. Passing rejects answer-span head truncation as the dominant explanation for this failure cluster and routes the next experiment to query/document semantic alignment; failing admits, but does not validate, an auditable passage-dense candidate.
changed_mechanisms: retrieval-input provenance and tokenizer-window visibility audit
anti_claim: This is a frozen-artifact diagnostic, not training, retrieval improvement, or a model-capability improvement.

framework_comparisons.current_gap: Delegation cannot repair an answer span removed before document embedding, and adding roles would hide rather than identify this representation boundary.
Research compression occurs after retrieval; the cheaper prior question is whether the retriever representation could see the answer span at all.
More crawling changes corpus breadth, but all seven cases already have answer-bearing gold documents locally; representation visibility is the smaller causal question.
Parallel search cannot establish whether a fixed dense index discarded answer-bearing document tails during encoding.

next_action: Implement and run the zero-provider 4096-token document visibility audit. If at least 4/7 cases are visible, reject truncation as the dominant explanation and preregister the simplest query/document semantic-alignment diagnostic before typed linking or passage-dense indexing.
claim_boundary: Passing or failing this posthoc audit changes only the next diagnostic route. It does not establish exact historical prebuilt-index preprocessing, retrieval effectiveness, answer quality, official accuracy, leaderboard rank, or model capability improvement.
